title: Best Gyms in Wellington 2026 — CBD, Hutt Valley, and Kapiti
meta_desc: Explore the best gyms in Wellington 2026 – from CBD premium clubs to Hutt Valley value hubs and Kapiti local gyms. Real prices, contracts, and Les Mills alternatives.
intro: Wellington’s gym scene is split between high‑end boutique clubs in the CBD and community‑focused facilities in the Hutt Valley and Kapiti. Knowing the exact weekly cost and contract terms can save you hundreds a year.

sections.heading: Wellington gym landscape 2026
sections.body: The capital now hosts three clear tiers: premium chains (mainly Les Mills) in the city centre, mid‑range 24/7 gyms with limited classes, and low‑cost community clubs that focus on equipment. Most providers still require a 12‑month minimum contract with a $100 exit fee, though many allow three months of freeze per year.

sections.heading: Price comparison – weekly cost and contract terms
Les Mills vs alternatives – what’s the real difference
sections.body: Les Mills gyms charge a premium for a constantly refreshed class schedule (e.g., BODYCOMBAT, RPM, PIIT28) and world‑class instructors. Cheaper 24/7 gyms give you the same equipment but limited or no group sessions, meaning you’ll need to plan your own workouts.
list: Class variety – Les Mills offers 30+ weekly classes; most alternatives offer 2‑4.
Cost – Les Mills averages $50 /week versus $10‑$14 for 24/7 gyms.
Flexibility – 24/7 gyms let you train any hour without a class slot.
Community – Les Mills cultivates a class‑based community; budget gyms rely on self‑motivation.
